nodes.description: The loss-of-function ANK mouse. nodes.description: Independently of inflammation, CPP crystals have direct catabolic effects on chondrocytes and synoviocytes, eliciting matrix metalloproteinases and prostaglandins, and deposits alter the mechanical properties of cartilage. The result is a chronic, polyarticular, osteoarthritis-like arthropathy with unusually severe articular damage, which in familial disease begins decades earlier than sporadic CPPD. Whether crystals cause or follow the cartilage degradation is not settled in sporadic disease; the early-onset familial form argues for crystals first.

nodes.description: Pyrophosphate in cartilage is normally generated from extracellular ATP by ENPP1 and degraded by alkaline phosphatase; at physiological levels it inhibits hydroxyapatite formation. In CCAL2 the exporter pushes matrix PPi above the concentration at which it instead precipitates with calcium. Lymphocytes and fibroblasts from familial CPPD patients also carry high PPi, so the excess is systemic even though the deposits are articular.

nodes.description: ANK sits in the chondrocyte plasma membrane and exports intracellular PPi into the matrix. Chondrocytes expressing CCAL2-mutant ANK release more extracellular PPi than cells expressing wild-type ANK, most consistently for P5L; the 5'-UTR and E490del variants also increase ANKH translation in vitro, so part of the effect may be more protein rather than a faster transporter. Later work models ANK as also mediating ATP efflux, with extracellular ENPP1 converting the ATP to pyrophosphate; by either route the net output of the node is more matrix pyrophosphate.
